title: Sampled-token prioritization for tail mitigation and kernel-aware routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a lightweight sampled-token prioritization layer in the admission path that estimates per-request decode cost from the prefill stream and uses that estimate to shape continuous batches, route to kernel profiles, and reserve decode slots. Goal is to reduce 99th percentile decode latency for mixed-length workloads while preserving overall throughput and unit cost.
background: We continue to observe tail amplification in mixed workloads where many short inference requests are delayed behind large, long-decode requests. Previous mitigations (static slot reservation and simple size buckets) reduce worst-case tails but either waste capacity or negatively impact throughput. This ticket explores a probabilistic estimator that samples token statistics from the prefill and early decode, enabling finer-grained admission decisions and kernel routing without a full per-request profiling pass.
proposed_solution:
1) Add a sampled-token estimator that reads the first N tokens of the prefill (configurable, default N=8) and computes a compact signature: estimated total decode tokens, entropy of token-type distribution, and presence of patterns that historically correlate with long decodes (e.g., long code blocks or dense punctuation).
2) Use the signature to assign a prioritization score and a kernel affinity label (low-latency kernel vs throughput kernel vs fallback quantized kernel).
3) Admission controller uses soft-priority queues with probabilistic coalescing: high-priority (short estimated decode) requests are admitted immediately into micro-batches up to a micro-batch cap; long-estimate requests are staged into shapeable batches where the controller opportunistically fills with short requests via coalescing heuristics.
4) Kernel router maps affinity label to a small set of kernels selected by offline profiling for those signature clusters; if chosen kernel capacity is saturated, route to compatible kernel variants or apply graceful degradation (e.g., smaller model variant) according to policy.
5) Implement lightweight attention fast-path hinting: when the estimator detects dense attention patterns, enable an attention-optimized kernel path (e.g., fused attention for token spans) to reduce per-token compute.
design_decisions:
- Estimator must be sub-millisecond and run on the request-handling CPU path; no GPU introspection.
- Use sampling window of 8 tokens to balance estimator accuracy vs overhead; make window configurable via feature flag.
- Soft-priority admission (probabilistic) rather than strict preemption to avoid starvation.
- Kernel affinity labels are approximate and used as hints; scheduler retains final authority based on real-time queue congestion.
tradeoffs:
- Risk: estimator misclassification could route short requests to throughput kernels increasing latency; mitigated by continuous feedback and exponential smoothing of scores.
- Complexity: adds additional routing dimension which increases scheduling state; we limit cardinality of affinity labels to keep scheduler complexity low.
- Cost: aggressive prioritization may slightly reduce realized GPU utilization; acceptance criteria constrain throughput/cost regression.
acceptance_criteria:
- On our mixed-length benchmark (token-length distribution 8/32/128/512 in 45/30/20/5 ratio): 99th-percentile decode latency reduced by >=25% compared to baseline runtime-1.21 continuous-batcher, while overall token throughput drop is <=3% and cost-per-1M-tokens changes by <=2%.
- No increase in tail error rates (time-outs, OOMs) beyond baseline.
- Feature gated and default-off in production; canary shows stable behavior across three independent clusters for 48h before ramp.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for estimator: accuracy against labeled dataset of prefill prefixes.
- Integration tests: synthetic traffic generator that emits mixed distributions and validates admission behavior (queue lengths, micro-batch fill rates).
- Perf tests: run A/B perf jobs against runtime-1.21 baseline for 24-hour window capturing p50/p90/p95/p99 and throughput.
- Chaos test: simulate kernel capacity loss and verify graceful routing/fallback and that high-priority traffic stays within latency SLOs.
rollout_plan:
- Implement behind feature flag.
- Stage 1 (dev): run in local and staging clusters, run integration/perf jobs.
- Stage 2 (canary): enable for 5% of hostnames in a dedicated canary cluster for 48h while running perf and error monitors.
- Stage 3 (regional ramp): expand to 20% of traffic across two regions for 72h, monitor recovery and metrics.
- Stage 4 (global): full rollout if metrics pass.
